description.narrative:
Impact objective:
All citizens and organizations in BiH access and benefit from transparent, fair, and democratic services based on accurate land, real estate and geospatial information provided by the Geodetic Authorities in cooperation with key stakeholders.
Outcome objectives per component:
Overall Capacity Development: Geodetic Agencies (GAs) are modern, transparent and efficient organizations contributing to economic and social development in close cooperation with stakeholders involved in land administration in BiH.
Mass Valuation: GAs contribute to a transparent property market by managing a real estate mass valuation system to benefit all citizens and the business community.
Spatial Data Infrastructure (SDI): GAs and other spatial data providers enable service-based sharing of up-to-date and accurate spatial data used by stakeholders to face and resolve sustainable development challenges.
Geodetic Infrastructure: The accurate, reliable, and easily accessible geodetic infratructure is globally integrated and used by all stakeholders.

Detta projekt är utvecklat gemensamt av Federal Administration for Geodetic and Real Property Affairs (FGA) i Bosnien och Hercegovina (FBiH), Republic Authority for Geodetic and Property Legal Affairs (RGA) i Republika Srpska (RS) och Lantmäteriet i samarbete med Skatteverket.
De förväntade resultaten av projektet är: Övergripande kapacitetsutveckling: GA är moderna, transparenta och effektiva organisationer som bidrar till ekonomisk och social utveckling i nära samarbete med intressenter som är involverade i markförvaltningen i Bosnien och Hercegovina.
Massvärdering: GA bidrar till en transparent fastighetsmarknad genom att hantera ett massvärderingssystem för fastigheter till nytta för alla medborgare och näringslivet.
Spatial Data Infrastructure (SDI): GA och andra rumsliga dataleverantörer möjliggör tjänstebaserad delning av aktuell och korrekt rumslig data som används av intressenter för att möta och lösa utmaningar inom hållbar utveckling.
Geodetisk infrastruktur: Den exakta, pålitliga och lättillgängliga geodetiska infrastrukturen är globalt integrerad och används av alla intressenter. .

This project is developed jointly by Federal Administration for Geodetic and Real Property Affairs (FGA) of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina (FBiH), Republic Authority for Geodetic and Property Legal Affairs (RGA) of the Republika Srpska (RS) and Lantmäteriet, The Swedish Mapping, Cadastral and Land Registration Authority in cooperation with the Swedish Tax Agency.
The expected outcomes of the project are: Overall Capacity Development: GA are modern, transparent and efficient organiza-tions contributing to economic and social development in close cooperation with stake-holders involved in land administration in BiH.
Mass Valuation: GA contribute to a transparent property market by managing a real estate mass valuation system to benefit all citizens and the business community.
Spatial Data Infrastructure (SDI): GA and other spatial data providers enable service-based sharing of up-to-date and accurate spatial data used by stakeholders to face and resolve sustainable development challenges.
Geodetic Infrastructure: The accurate, reliable, and easily accessible geodetic infra-structure is globally integrated and used by all stakeholders.

The reports indicated progress in strengthened technical and institutional readiness across both geodetic authorities. 1. Improved institutional behaviour and cooperation The project has contributed to a measurable improvement in cooperation between FGA and RGA. Joint study visits, shared training, and coordinated SDI activities have created habits of collaboration that were not present at the start of the intervention. This behavioural shift is significant in a politically fragmented environment and increases the likelihood of harmonised land administration practices across entities. 2. Increased technical autonomy and reduced dependency FGAs ability to independently run Bernese (a positioning software) application represents a step change in technical autonomy. This reduces reliance on external contractors and strengthens the sustainability of geodetic infrastructure. The same trajectory is expected for RGA as training is completed in early 2026. 3. Strengthened enabling environment for future reforms Progress in SDI including draft implementation rules, stakeholder training, and improved communication structures is beginning to create the conditions required for interoperable spatial data. This is a critical prerequisite for mass valuation, evidencebased planning, and transparent land markets. The fact that SDI stakeholders have already participated in 20 oneday trainings indicates a widening circle of institutions now capable of contributing to a national SDI. 4. Enhanced analytical capacity for mass valuation Both entities now demonstrate improved capacity to conduct zoning, market analysis, and data preparation. This represents a shift in the respective authorities ability to understand and interpret property markets, which is essential for transparent valuation systems. The integration of Slovenian expertise has accelerated this shift by providing regionally relevant methodologies. 5. Increased institutional preparedness and resilience Despite extreme turnover, the project has managed to rebuild consultant teams, introduce new coordinators, and maintain core functions. This demonstrates increased organisational resilience and the ability to absorb shocks which is an important impact in itself in a volatile administrative environment. 6. Early signs of improved stakeholder trust and engagement The SDI Days and expanded training programmes have increased visibility and understanding of geospatial data among external stakeholders. This is an early indicator of improved trust and a more service oriented approach within the geodetic authorities. 7. Integration with the World Bank project is back on track after delays in RGA The project has also adapted its approach to mass valuation by integrating Slovenian expertise and aligning more closely with the World Bank GIVE project. Staff at both FGA and RGA have adopted new tools, standards, and workflows (e.g. GNSS, SDI, and mass valuation zoning
